usageNotes: Use this to remove a specific IP address or CIDR block from a cluster-level firewall IPSet. The caller must hold the Sys.Modify privilege on the root path (/). Pass the current configuration digest to guard against concurrent edits overwriting each other — omitting it skips the optimistic-lock check. This operation is synchronous and returns null on success; the firewall rule referencing this IPSet takes effect immediately after removal.

examples.summary: Remove a specific host IP from the 'trusted-mgmt' IPSet

destructiveReason: Permanently removes the specified IP/CIDR entry from the IPSet; any firewall rules that allowed or denied traffic based on this entry will stop matching that address immediately.
tips: Fetch the current digest via GET /cluster/firewall/ipset/{name} before deleting to avoid optimistic-lock conflicts in automation scripts.
The 'cidr' path param accepts bare IPs (e.g. 10.0.0.1), CIDR notation (e.g. 10.0.0.0/24), or an alias name — match exactly what is stored in the IPSet.
Removing an entry from an IPSet that is actively referenced by cluster firewall rules takes effect instantly; verify no production traffic depends on the entry before deleting.
